records.finding: Added a transmission event documenting that cultivated maize of Mesoamerican ancestry had reached the Peruvian coast by the dated Paredones specimen. That evidence leaves the Xihuatoxtla donor and its connection to either Nahua nixtamalization or Wari brewing unresolved. Neither a common crop name nor a shared region documents grain supply.

sources.note: Par_N1 has directly dated attached husk and shank, and the genetic comparison tests the cob itself. The age is also reported by the earlier excavators and is one specimen determination.
Accepted manuscript. Independent archaeological and landrace genome set supports movement out of Mexico. Interpretations differ on whether traits were already fixed.
Grobman et al. report the same Paredones specimen, so this is not another date.

sources.note: The existing Nahua candidate concerns the supply in a particular later setting.

records.next: Seek ancient DNA connecting particular Mesoamerican source populations to dated recipient grains and evidence for processing or supply into named historical settings.

records.finding: Refined Phase II-2 use and material evidence: laminated natural clay distinguishes the blocks from later tempered adobe. Earlier clay building practice, including reported Ñanchoc hut-foundation blocks, offers comparison only. The catalogued coastal platform-and-plaza tradition is broader and differs from the local room.

records.finding: Distinguished the directly dated 5440–5310 cal BP residue PLD-005 from the much later cacao-positive funerary bottles. Retained the broader priority question and deferred regional transmission because the evidence does not isolate the transfer of a particular crop or preparation technique.

Chemical support for local Puerto Escondido use. No ancestry connection to this Ecuadorian site.

records.next: Seek cacao-positive vessels with secure specimen-level dates and comparable ancient genetic markers across intervening sites. Distinguish movement of planting stock from exchange of beverages or preparation knowledge.

records.finding: Retained the existing Canal 3 candidate. The hydraulic calculations use a probable common lower-bench destination. Earlier probable garden furrows are at a different fan, and later regional canal systems do not establish continuity. Added the distinction between modeling and tracing an outlet.

records.finding: Located both earliest crop indicators at Isla Manechi. Squash phytolith size falls in a domesticated range, while the authors leave local domestication versus adoption open. Anthropogenic island deposition and garden location are separate claims. Similar early manioc exploitation at Real Alto or later cassava pressing does not identify planting stock from this particular site.

sources.note: Bern repository accepted manuscript. Early manioc identification is one heart-shaped phytolith. The possible gardens are inferred.

sources.note: Overlapping investigators provide site sediment and shell evidence. The principal site differs from the earliest Isla Manechi crop locality.
Independent modern genetic evidence favours domestication along the southern Amazon margin. The sampled genealogy cannot identify an ancient Isla Manechi donor.

records.next: Find an early planting surface or a diagnostic larger assemblage at Isla Manechi. Trace dated and independently sampled populations between this site and later manioc-processing localities.

records.finding: Retained the existing Tierra Blanca–Canal 3 candidate and sharpened its finding. The Las Pircas dental samples are earlier, and Tierra Blanca botanical remains from sites such as CA-09-71 do not locate a crop in the undated lower-bench field. Channel and field association remains unresolved.

Teeth document Las Pircas consumption. Later cultivation context is synthesis by the same project.
Dated cotton is from a house floor. This is not independent proof of irrigation or crop identity in the field.

records.next: Locate the outlet and dated field horizon. Sample it for crop indicators independent of the earlier dental or household materials.

records.finding: Revised the local event to report the layer IV estimate and the later inference of greater management of vicuña-like camelids. The new talus and isotopic evidence challenges the older domestic-phenotype interpretation and leaves restriction method unresolved. A modern documented Cotahuasi pack-llama use is no evidence of descent from this rock shelter.

records.finding: Retained the directly dated stratum 52 cotton yarn as an independent finding. The later stratum 44 cloth directly demonstrates the use of plied cotton yarn, while the connection to the earlier yarn-making tradition remains a candidate. The analytical reports share an analyst and assemblage.
